dialect.detail: NEASI-WEBER ADMARC system (Advertising Management and Accounts Receivable Control), customized for New York Times. Uses vendor-specific COPY members (AMZFSTD, AMZRSEL, AMZMCOMP, etc.). Likely runs on a mid-range or PC-based COBOL environment given LINE SEQUENTIAL organization and no COMP-3 usage.

purpose.domain_detail: Advertising billing and accounts receivable for New York Times newspaper. Prints invoices from a select file of work orders, groups open items by account, and produces lockbox, settlement, credit card, FTP, and mag-tape output files.
purpose.summary: AMOFLPRG is the invoice printing program of the ADMARC advertising management system, customized for the New York Times. It reads a select file of work order records (produced by a selection program), groups them by account, and prints invoices while also generating lockbox, settlement, credit card, FTP transfer, and magnetic tape output files. It includes ACR (accounts receivable control) include/exclude logic and handles unpaid/pending work orders.

notable_features: Multiple output file types: lockbox, settlement, credit card reports, FTP, mag-tape, invoice
Indexed file access (Cc-Det-Bin-File with RECORD KEY)
COPY-based configuration (AMZMCOMP, AMZMSPEC, AMZFSTD, AMZRSEL, etc.)
Change log with programmer initials in column 73 (NYT convention)
99 CALL statements indicating heavy subprogram use
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
No COMP-3 usage despite financial application
verdict.notes: Source is truncated to first 16000 chars out of 623KB/9243 lines. The change log references releases from 1983-1985 through at least 2007 (CTS changes), indicating decades of maintenance. Sequence numbers in columns 1-6 are non-standard (e.g. 'AL-03', 'DW-08', 'FXC---') used as change tags rather than numeric sequence numbers, which is unusual but consistent with a heavily modified legacy system. No COMP-3 is notable for a financial system; numeric fields use display or COMP binary.
